The present petition under Section 482 of the CrPC seeks quashing of the FIR No. 187/2020,
under Sections 498A/360/34 of the IPC, registered at P.S. Lajpat Nagar.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
2. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that during the pendency of the investigation in the aforesaid FIR, the latter has entered into settlement agreement with the complainant, who is the brother of the petitioner's deceased wife.
It is pointed out that the present FIR was registered at the instance of respondent no. 2, who in pursuance of the aforesaid settlement agreement dated 30.06.2023 has no objection if the present FIR and the consequent proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
opennyai_summary.19_September_2023__ANALYSIS:
As per the status report dated 12.09.2023 authored by Insp. Satya Prakash, SHO/Lajpat Nagar,
the present FIR was initially registered under Sections 498A/306/34 of the IPC and during the course of further investigation, Sections 304B/406 of the IPC have also been added.
5. The present petition has been filed purely on the basis of a compromise between the complainant,
i.e., brother of the deceased and the petitioner.
6. Honble Supreme Court, in Narinder Singh & Ors v. State of Punjab & Anr., (2014) 6 SCC 466 has held that although the High Courts have an inherent power under Section 482 of the CrPC to quash proceedings on the basis of a compromise, however, in case of heinous offences which are generally treated as crimes against the society, quashing of the offences in view of the settlement would not be permissible.
The offences alleged in the present FIR include Sections 306 and 304B of the IPC.
Looking at the nature of the offences, the settlement cannot be a ground for quashing of the present FIR and the consequent proceedings thereto.
opennyai_summary.19_September_2023__decision:
7. In view thereof, the present petition is dismissed and disposed of accordingly.
8. Pending application(s), if any, also stand disposed of.
